title: Crispy Roast Potatoes
subtitle: Floury potatoes parboiled, roughed up, and roasted until shatteringly crisp
excerpt: The technique is the recipe here: parboil until the edges begin to fluff, drain and shake hard to roughen the surface, then drop into very hot fat. That rough, steamed surface is what becomes the crust.
sourceNotes: Crispy roast potatoes are an essential element of the British Sunday roast. The technique of parboiling before roasting is the defining step that separates great roasties from mediocre ones.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Parboil and roughen the potatoes up to 4 hours ahead. Keep uncovered in the fridge so the surface dries out: they will be even crispier.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 200C / Gas 7. The oven must be at temperature before you add the potatoes.

content.text: The fat in the roasting tin must be very hot before the potatoes go in. If you add potatoes to cold fat they absorb it and become greasy rather than crisp. You should hear a loud sizzle the moment they touch the tin.

items.prepNote: floury variety, peeled and cut into large chunks (about 6cm)

content.text: Put the sunflower oil in the roasting tin. Place in the oven and preheat to 220C. The oil needs at least 15 minutes to get properly hot.
Put the potatoes in a large saucepan. Cover with cold, well-salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the edges are beginning to look fluffy.
Drain thoroughly in a colander. Leave to steam for 2 minutes. Shake the colander vigorously several times so the edges break up and look rough and shaggy.
Carefully tip the potatoes into the very hot oil. They will spit. Turn each piece to coat fully in the oil. Add the garlic and rosemary.
Roast for 25 minutes without moving. Turn each potato, then roast for another 25 to 30 minutes until deeply golden and crisp all over.
Season with flaky salt immediately after coming out of the oven. Serve at once.

items.symptom: The potatoes are not crispy, just soft and oily.
items.cause: The fat was not hot enough before the potatoes were added.
items.fix: Return to the oven at maximum heat for 15 more minutes.

items.symptom: The potatoes are sticking to the tin.
items.cause: They were turned too early before the crust had formed.
items.fix: Leave them undisturbed for the full 25 minutes before the first turn.

items.symptom: The edges are crisp but the centre is hard.
items.fix: Next time, parboil until you can see visible fluffing at the edges.
